answers.q1: Ruby with Bundler (Gemfile at the root, plus separate Gemfiles in sinatra-contrib and rack-protection). Install with: bundle install. CI also runs `bundle install` inside sinatra-contrib: (cd sinatra-contrib && bundle install).
answers.q2: Core sinatra suite, which is what CI runs from the root: bundle exec rake (the default task is `test`, a Minitest::TestTask). CI also runs the other two packages separately: (cd rack-protection && bundle install && bundle exec rake) and (cd sinatra-contrib && bundle install && bundle exec rake). The sinatra-contrib Rakefile runs rspec.
answers.q3: cd sinatra-contrib && bundle exec rspec spec/capture_spec.rb. This is rspec, not Minitest, and the sinatra-contrib Gemfile and .rspec are in that directory. Equivalent from the root: bundle exec rspec --default-path sinatra-contrib/spec sinatra-contrib/spec/capture_spec.rb. That form is untested and may not pick up sinatra-contrib's Gemfile or .rspec. The cd form is safer.
answers.q4: No workflow in .github/workflows runs rubocop or any other lint step, so CI doesn't check lint. The only lint config is .rubocop.yml, and rubocop ~> 1.32.0 is in the root Gemfile. Run it locally from the root with: bundle exec rubocop. The config excludes test/**, rack-protection/**, and sinatra-contrib/**.
answers.q5: No committed generated or vendored code that I found. Don't hand-edit these git-ignored or generated paths: coverage/ (from `rake test:coverage`), doc/ and doc/api (from yardoc), .yardoc, pkg/, *.gem, *.lock (Gemfile.lock), .bundle, and vendor/ (including vendor/bundle). The block between the `agentbrief:start` and `agentbrief:end` markers in AGENTS.md is also generated by `agentbrief sync`, so don't edit it.
